Shri A.N. Gupta - Government Advocate for the respondent
Shri Neeraj Shah - Advocate for the objector.
Heard on I.A.No. 297 of 2023 application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellants Ramchandra Gaderi and Shyambihari @ Bihari Saha.

The appellant No.1 has been convicted under Section 342 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I for 1 year with fine of Rs. 1,000/-, under Section 376(D) of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years with fine of Rs.5,000/- and under Section 376(D) of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years with fine of Rs.5,000/- , under Section 506-II of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I for 5 years with fine of Rs. 2,000/-, under Section 506-II of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I for 5 years with fine of Rs. 2,000/- and under Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989 and sentenced to life imprisonment with fine of Rs. 10,000/-, with default stipulations.

The appellant No.2 has been convicted under Section 342/120-B of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I for 1 year with fine of Rs. 1,000/-, under Section 376(D) of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years with fine of Rs.5,000/-, under Section 376(D) of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years with fine of Rs.5,000/- , under Section 506-II of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I for 5 years with fine of Rs. 2,000/-, and under Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act 1989 and sentenced to life imprisonment with fine of Rs. 10,000/-,with default stipulations.
It is common ground taken by counsel for the appellants that incident had taken place in two spells.

As per prosecution story on 27.10.2017, a report was lodged in police station Langhadool that Ms.
"A" in the month of June 2017 called the victim, took her to the courtyard where appellant No. 2 was present.
The victim was taken inside the house and thereafter door was closed from outside.
In the house, the appellant No. 1 was present who sexually assaulted her.
The second spell relates to the date i.e. 14.10.2017 when appellant No. 2 allegedly sexually assaulted the victim.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for appellants submits that there is inordinate delay in lodging the report.

The mother of victim (PW/2) admitted that on the date of second incident i.e.
14.10.2017 itself the victim informed her about commission of offence.
However, the FIR was lodged belatedly on 27.10.2017.
Neither MLC nor FSL/DNA report supports the case of prosecution.
The whole case of prosecution is based on ocular evidence of the prosecutrix.
It is common ground that the statement of prosecutrix is not of 'sterling' quality.
Thus conviction founded upon such statement is vulnerable and liable to be interfered with.

To elaborate it is urged that mother of victim (PW/2) in para 16 of her cross examination categorically admitted that there existed previous enmity regarding picking of "Mahua" from a tree and regarding a land dispute between the appellants and the family of victim.
It is further informed that the victim herself admitted that she had taken Rs. 2,00,000/- as victim compensation arising out of the FIR in question.

By taking this Court to another judgment passed in ST No. 7/19 decided on 13.05.20, it is pointed out that the same victim as per the prosecution story mentioned therein travelled on a motor cycle with the appellant no. 1 and victim got Rs. 3,00,000/-
as compensation.

It is submitted that if story of prosecution is correct and appellant No. 1 sexually assaulted the victim, there was no occasion for her to again take lift from appellant Ramchandra and travel to Gajra Bajra.
Thus story of prosecution is like house of cards and conviction is based on surmises and conjectures.
T h e prayer is opposed by learned Government Advocate for the respondent- State on the strength of objection.

The counsel for objector during the course of argument submits that he has no objection if the sentence is suspended for appellant No. 1 although for appellant No. 2 he took a diametrically opposite stand.

Considering the aforesaid factual backdrop a clear case is made out for suspending the remaining jail sentence of the appellants, therefore, without expressing any conclusive opinion on merits of the case, I.A.No. 297/2023 is allowed.

Subject to depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited), the remaining jail sentence of the appellants are hereby suspended and it is directed that on furnishing personal bond for a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees thirty Thousand Only) each along with one surety in the like amount each to the satisfaction of the trial Court by the appellants, they be released on bail with a further direction to remain present before the concerned Trial Court - Waidhan District Singrauli on 11 th March, 2024 and on such other dates as may be fixed by the trial court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
